we have developed a new imaging method for 3D representation of the diatom frustules, by combining two microscopy techniques.

we have developed an innovative methodology for the generation of 3D diatom replicas, which is based on the merging of two different imaging techniques, namely scanning electron microscopy and atomic force microscopy or digital holography, and that the proposed approach is of great interest in the fabrication of photonic devices.

the development of new methods for the characterization and simulation of the optical properties of diatoms.
the development of novel methods to characterize the optical and mechanical behavior of microstructures, and with the development of new fabrication methods for optical microdevices.
the development of novel imaging methods for the characterization of micro-optical components.

the method here presented allows a 3D reconstruction of the object, starting from the analysis of two digital images, with high resolution in the three spatial directions.
the developed methodology is a very powerful tool for the study of micro- and nanoscale structures and for the development of novel optical devices.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new method for generating high spatial resolution three-dimensional (3d) model of diatoms, by merging scanning-electron microscopy (sem) and digital holographic microscopy (dhm) or atomic-force microscopy (afm) data.

we have been able to reconstruct a three-dimensional model of diatom valve with a high degree of spatial resolution, which is comparable or even superior to that obtained with the most advanced techniques.
we developed a new method that merges two digital images, each of which was acquired separately with standard characterisation procedures, to obtain a 3D model with a high spatial resolution.

the combination of different microscopy techniques allows to overcome the intrinsic limits and to improve the spatial resolution of a single microscopy technique, generating 3D images of the object with very high definition.
